title_as_printed: Table III. Mean Values of the Experimental Henry's Law Constant, k, for Methane
henry_definition: Modified Henry's law constant k = phi P / x = gamma k0 (eq 2), in MPa. phi = fugacity coefficient of methane at reactor temperature and TOTAL reactor pressure (generalized chart, Smith and Van Ness 1959); P = methane partial pressure = reactor pressure minus the vapour pressure of water over the brine (Haas 1976 reference-substance technique, used for SSGB as well); x = mole fraction of methane in the brine at reactor conditions, eq 3: x = m / (m + sum_j m_j sum_i nu_ij + 1000/M), m = methane molality, m_j = molality of salt j, nu_ij = moles of ionic species i per mole of salt j (salts counted as dissociated ions), M = molecular weight of water. For pure water k equals the true Henry constant k0 = f/a (eq 1, standard state methane at infinite dilution in water); for brines k includes the methane activity coefficient gamma. Each printed k is the mean of four to eight experimental values at one test condition.
pressure_note: Printed P column is the total reactor pressure (footnote a). The methane partial pressure used in k was computed by the author as reactor pressure minus water vapour pressure over the brine (not printed).

value.what: modified Henry's law constant k = phi*P_CH4/x (see henry_definition); mean of 4-8 determinations

composition.other_species: Blocks: water (salt-free); NaCl-1..NaCl-4 (NaCl only, molality from Table I); SSGB = synthetic Salton Sea geothermal brine (alkali and alkaline-earth metal chlorides; composition in ppm by weight in Table II: Ba 207, B 324, Ca 23900, Cs 17, Cl 129000, Fe 1660, Pb 66, Li 174, Mg 8, Mn 1140, K 13700, Rb 58, silica 332, Na 44000, Sr 365, S 25, Zn 415; total molality 4.05 m, molarity 3.55 M, ionic strength 6.18 per Table I; salt concentrations 17 % lower than the unflashed IID-2 brine, Cu and Ag omitted, pH adjusted to neutral with small additions of NaOH).

skip_rows.reason: block label rows (water, NaCl-1, NaCl-2, NaCl-3, NaCl-4, SSGB)

sets.value: SSGB synthetic Salton Sea geothermal brine: Table I molality 4.05 m, molarity 3.55 M, ionic strength 6.18 (molal); element composition in ppm by weight in Table II (table_II.csv)

row_held.reason: footnote b: k values computed by Cramer from the published solubility data of Culberson and McKetta (1951), not measured in this work (text: 'Six additional values, computed from published methane solubility data (Culberson and McKetta, 1951) for water at temperatures from 25 to 171.1 C'); from_literature

conversion_needs: k to mole fraction: x = phi * P_CH4 / k needs the methane fugacity coefficient at T and total P and the methane partial pressure (total P minus water vapour pressure over the brine); neither is printed. x is on a dissociated-ion basis (eq 3).
C to K: + 273.15 (lowest printed T 0.5 C, NaCl-2; no row below 273.15 K).
SSGB composition is given as element ppm by weight (Table II), not as salts; conversion to salt molalities needs an ion-to-salt assignment and is not given by the author.
notes: Six side-by-side blocks printed in two bands of three (water, NaCl-1, NaCl-2 / NaCl-3, NaCl-4, SSGB); stacked in reading order, one label row per block. Thousands separators printed as thin spaces (e.g. '2 580') are removed in the CSV (2580). Rows are not in strictly increasing T in some blocks (NaCl-2 12.6 then 13.0; NaCl-3 205.3 after 203.7 with higher k); kept as printed. Footnote-b rows (water block, 6 rows) are from the literature and held.
